title: Clockwork Knight 2
subtitle: Another night for Pepper
summary: Clockwork Knight 2 is Sega's platform sequel, first released for Saturn in Japan on 28 July 1995.
body: Clockwork Knight 2 is Sega's platform sequel, first released for Saturn in Japan on 28 July 1995. It continues the first game's ending: Chelsea has returned but remains asleep, and another abduction sends Pepper after her again. The toy knight still fights with his key and moves through household environments whose scale makes him vulnerable to ordinary objects. New rooms and more varied stage sequences expand the journey, retaining the mixture of pre-rendered characters and polygonal scenery that gave the original its miniature theatrical appearance.

Four playing cards are hidden in each main level. Finding all four earns a gold key, while collecting the full set of thirty-two provides a level-selection code. Those rewards give the room's concealed passages a purpose beyond an immediate life or score bonus. Some stages carry Pepper forward automatically, changing the pace of the platforming. Others let him ride his donkey Barobaro, whose detachable head can be launched at enemies. The familiar key attack therefore shares the adventure with new ways to move and clear a path.

Hidden obstacle races provide additional challenges, while the North American edition includes Bosses Galore, a mode drawn from the Japanese compilation of both games. Pepper or Ginger can face bosses from the two adventures and receive a ranking for their performance. The main journey moves through a child's room, a study, a bathroom and a clock tower, giving the sequel a different set of household objects to transform. Its strongest additions reward returning to those spaces, finding the concealed cards and learning the short sequences that make each room work.
story_headings: A reason to search the room
